sources.entry: django-compressor - Compresses linked and inline JavaScript or CSS into a single cached file.

summary.one_liner: Django Compressor is a Django library that processes, combines and minifies linked and inline JavaScript or CSS in templates into cacheable static files.
summary.what_it_does: The {% compress js/css %} template tag wraps linked and inline CSS or JS, which is then processed by optional compilers and filters. The default CSS filter rewrites static file paths to absolute, and JS and CSS are concatenated and minified by default. The tag outputs a script or link tag pointing to the optimized file, or can inline the result into the page. File names depend on content, so files can get far-future expiry dates. The manage.py compress command can run the build outside the request cycle. The README names support for CoffeeScript, LESS and SASS compilers, plus YUI, yUglify, Google Closure Compiler, JSMin, csscompressor, and a data URI image filter. HTML parsing uses lxml, Python's HTMLParser, BeautifulSoup or html5lib.
use_cases: minify and combine CSS and JavaScript in Django templates
compile LESS, SASS or CoffeeScript within Django pages
precompile static assets with a management command
inline small images as data URIs in CSS
how_to_run: Wrap CSS/JS in templates with {% compress js %} or {% compress css %} and {% endcompress %}
python manage.py compress (optional, to run the build ahead of time)
notable: Content-hashed output filenames allow far-future cache expiry
Pluggable compilers and filters, with base classes for custom steps
Management command to precompile assets outside the request cycle
Choice of HTML parsers: lxml, HTMLParser, BeautifulSoup, html5lib
caveats: The README is partly stripped of links and badges, so some details such as the install command for the stable release are incomplete
Compilers such as LESS, SASS and Closure Compiler are external tools that the README implies must be set up separately
